correction.text: Wei Ao: 'independently controlled the modern eastern Gansu region, east of the Yellow River'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 25-34; no Cliopatria row. 'Wei, who independently controlled the modern eastern Gansu region, east of the Yellow River'; capital Luomen in modern Tianshui. The Tianshui and Pingliang circles stand for it; no page gives a frontier. No English Wikipedia article of his own was found ('Wei Xiao' and 'Wei Ao' do not exist).

region.text: Wei Ao: 'independently controlled the modern eastern Gansu region, east of the Yellow River'

ledger.note: 25: Wei Ao holds eastern Gansu, bridged. The page names Wei among the independent powers when Liu Xiu took the throne (summer 25) and dates none of his rise; the Gengshi page calls him a 'local warlord' whose strategist Fang Wang occupied Linjing in 25. PAGE SILENT. [Reviewer ea-02-x, 2026-10-19: counterpart changed from lulin (dossier ends 23) to han-dynasty, which carries the Gengshi regime of 23-25]

ledger.note: 30: the Eastern Han marches on Wei. 'started a campaign against Wei in the summer of AD 30'; Wei 'formally submitted to Gongsun and accepted a princely title, Prince of Shuoning, from him'.

ledger.note: 30: Wei submits to Gongsun Shu. 'Emperor Guangwu started a campaign against Wei in the summer of AD 30'; 'In response, Wei formally submitted to Gongsun and accepted a princely title, Prince of Shuoning, from him' (the sentence has no year of its own; 'in response' to the summer-30 campaign dates it to 30, confidence 2). Mirrors chengjia /ledger vassal_start 30 (added in the repair pass).

ledger.note: 34: the tie ends with the regime. 'In the winter of AD 34, Shuoning's capital Luomen fell, and Wei Chun surrendered' (Wei had died in AD 33); the page records no aid from Gongsun Shu in 31-34 and no separate end to the princely title.

notes:
Wei Ao (Wei Xiao), the Shuoning regime of eastern Gansu 25-34. 1 page used for events (Emperor Guangwu of Han), with the Gengshi Emperor page and the Longxi Commandery, Luomen (Wushan) pages opened and silent on him; Wei_Xiao, Wei_Ao and Dou_Rong (the last, a first time) returned URL_NOT_FOUND. Slug wei-ao follows the counterpart used in ea-02-c's han-dynasty dossier. Unsettled: start year (confidence 1); the extent (Tianshui, Longxi, Anding?); Wei's earlier service under Gengshi. Counterparts: han-dynasty and lulin exist; chengjia is written by this batch (its vassal tie: Wei submitted to Gongsun Shu in 30).
Repair pass (ea-02-x-fixed): vassal_start 30 and vassal_end 34 with chengjia added (Emperor Guangwu page, reopened: the submission sentence carries no year of its own, 'In response' to the summer-30 campaign), mirroring chengjia /ledger/3-4. The reviewer's counterpart fix (lulin to han-dynasty in /ledger/0) was already applied; the predecessor entry in identity is changed the same way, because lulin ends in 23.
